Buttons

Built-in appearances applied to Button: Accent for the primary action, Subtle for low-emphasis commands.
Place icons before or after text when the symbol helps the action scan faster.
Use HyperlinkButton for lightweight navigation and related secondary actions.
Use DropDownButton when all available actions live in the flyout.
Use SplitButton when there is one default action plus alternate actions in the flyout.
Use RepeatButton when holding the pointer should raise Click repeatedly.
Use ToggleButton when a command switches a state on or off and should look pressed while active.
Use ToggleSplitButton when the primary half toggles a state and the flyout chooses which variant of that state to apply.

Buttons
A simple Button with text content.
Selection
Use check boxes for independent options. Add three-state only when an indeterminate value has meaning.
Use radio buttons when people must choose exactly one option from a visible group.
Use toggle switches for settings that take effect immediately.
Use rating when a compact ordered preference is more natural than a numeric input.
Use a combo box when the choices are useful but do not need to stay visible.
Use toggle switches for settings that take effect immediately.
Inputs
Use text boxes for short text entry. Add icons, clear buttons, and limits when they clarify the expected input.
Show helper text for guidance and validation states for committed feedback.
Use AutoSuggestBox for search and autocomplete: handle TextChanged to filter suggestions and QuerySubmitted to act on the choice.
Use password boxes for protected text entry, with reveal and strength affordances when appropriate.
Use number boxes for numeric entry with optional spin buttons, bounds, and supporting descriptions.
Use sliders when a relative value is easier to choose visually than typing a precise number.
Use text boxes for short text entry. Add icons, clear buttons, and limits when they clarify the expected input.
Forms
Use TimePicker for choosing a time from hour, minute, and AM/PM columns in a flyout.
Use DatePicker for choosing a date from day, month, and year columns in a flyout.
Use ColorPicker for choosing a color from a saturation/value spectrum with a hue slider, alpha, RGB/HSV channel text input, and hex input.
Use a compact form for account access, with clear labels and a primary action.
Combine contact, shipping, and quantity fields when a form needs several related decisions.
Use form controls to edit a small set of preferences and show confirmation after saving.
Data
Use ListView for compact single-column collections and richer item layouts.
Set EmptyContent for an intentional no-data state and animate removals when items leave the list.
Use ListBox for compact selection lists; set SelectionMode to Extended to allow selecting multiple items.
Use PersonPicture to represent people and contact status in data-heavy views.
Use Card variants to group related data with different levels of visual emphasis.
Use Image to present pictures with a theme-aware stroke; CornerRadius drives the rounded clip from square to circular.
Set ItemsLayout to Grid when items read better as tiles that wrap across the list; List keeps one item per row.
Data binding
Add or remove items at runtime. The list updates through INotifyCollectionChanged.
Switch between Single, Multiple, and Extended selection modes.
Use an inline DataTemplate when every item shares the same row shape.
Trees
Use TreeViewItem nesting for compact folder, outline, or category hierarchies.
Handle SelectedItemChanged when selecting a node should update related content.
Use multiple selection when people need to select several nodes from the same hierarchy.
Set IsExpanded directly, or walk the item collection when a command controls the tree.
Menus
Use Menu for persistent command groups with submenus, keyboard cues, separators, and checked states.
Use ContextMenu for actions that apply to a selected item or region.
Use ToolTip for short hints that clarify icons, disabled commands, or risky actions.
Use Flyout for lightweight, light-dismiss popups (details, quick forms, confirmations) anchored to a control.
Use ContentDialog for modal prompts that require an explicit choice (confirmations, errors, sign-in).
Use TeachingTip for contextual, non-blocking coaching anchored to a UI element.
Use CommandBarFlyout for a compact command strip with an overflow menu; commands dismiss the flyout when invoked.

Flyout open
Command bar flyout open
Content dialog open
Navigation
Use a left pane for persistent destinations, with a header and separator to group the items.
Use top navigation for a small set of peer destinations that should leave the full width for content.
Use compact mode to preserve space, and enable the back button when the current view can navigate backward.
Use InfoBadge in NavigationViewItem to call attention to item state without changing the item label.
Use BreadcrumbBar to show the path to the current location and jump back to any ancestor.
Use PipsPager for compact page indication and switching, as in carousels and onboarding flows.
Use SelectorBar to switch between peer views of one page, and SlideNavigationPresenter to slide the view in from the side the selection moved.
Use PipsPager for compact page indication and switching, as in carousels and onboarding flows.
Tabs
Use TabControl for a small set of peer panels that share the same space.
Use TabStripPlacement to move the tab row when the layout benefits from a side rail.
Use TabView for document-style tabs with add and close affordances.
Use TabControl for a small set of peer panels that share the same space.
Layout
Use Border to frame a region, StackPanel spacing for readable rows, and Separator to divide related content.
Use DockPanel when one element should pin to an edge while the remaining content fills the available space.
Use Expander for secondary settings that should start collapsed until needed.
Use DockPanel inside Expander headers and content when the summary and secondary action need edge alignment.
Use SmoothScrollViewer for a constrained list; its Fluence scrollbar shows the scroll position.
Use Expander for secondary settings that should start collapsed until needed.
Use SmoothScrollViewer for a constrained list; its Fluence scrollbar shows the scroll position.
Status
Use ProgressBar for measurable work where the current value can be reported.
Use indeterminate mode when work is active but no reliable percentage is available.
Use step progress for ordered tasks where users understand the current milestone.
Use ProgressRing when space is tight or when progress belongs next to compact content.
Use InfoBar for inline messages that explain status, validation, or recoverable outcomes.
Use InfoBar for inline messages that explain status, validation, or recoverable outcomes.
Accessibility
Keyboard focus and explicit tab order.
High contrast remaps Fluence semantic brushes to Windows system colors.
Icon-only buttons expose AutomationProperties.Name for screen readers.
Right-to-left layout mirrors Fluence controls for RTL locales.
InfoBar and TextBox validation use LiveRegionChanged to announce status changes without interrupting the user.
RatingControl supports full keyboard navigation and exposes the RangeValue automation pattern.
